enonce_intro_markdown:
Sulphur dioxide reacts with air according to the equation below:

$2\mathrm{SO_2(g)} + \mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO_3(g)}$  $\Delta H = -196\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$
incertitudes: Le sujet se contredit : l'en-tête de la page de garde demande 4 questions sur 5 en Section A, mais le titre de la Section A dit « Answer ALL questions in this section ». La règle de l'en-tête est retenue.
Points imprimés 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10 : cohérents avec « Total 10 marks ».
La valeur de l'énergie est imprimée « -196 KJ/mol » : recopiée en kJ/mol.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Explain the meaning of $\Delta H = -196$ kJ/mol.

(ii) State two (2) reaction conditions for the above reaction. *[3 marks]*

(i) State Le Chatelier's principle.

(ii) What will happen to the equilibrium position when

- pressure is increased?
- temperature is increased? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Le Chatelier's principle:** if a change (of temperature, pressure or concentration) is made to a system in dynamic equilibrium, the position of equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to **oppose (reduce) the change**.

(ii)

- **Pressure increased:** the equilibrium shifts to the **right**, towards $\mathrm{SO_3}$, because the forward reaction reduces the number of gas molecules (3 mol on the left, 2 mol on the right), which lowers the pressure. More $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is formed.
- **Temperature increased:** the equilibrium shifts to the **left**, because the backward reaction is endothermic and absorbs the added heat. Less $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is formed (the yield falls).

questions.enonce_markdown: What volume of oxygen is required to produce 300 cm$^3$ of $\mathrm{SO_3}$ at room temperature and pressure? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the equation, 1 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$ gives 2 mol $\mathrm{SO_3}$. Gas volumes measured under the same conditions are in the same ratio as the mole ratio, so:

volume of $\mathrm{O_2} = \dfrac{300}{2} = 150\ \mathrm{cm^3}$

(Check with the molar volume: $n(\mathrm{SO_3}) = \dfrac{300}{24000} = 0.0125$ mol; $n(\mathrm{O_2}) = \dfrac{0.0125}{2} = 0.00625$ mol; $V = 0.00625 \times 24000 = 150\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.)

**Answer: 150 cm$^3$ of oxygen.**

questions.enonce_markdown: State one environmental hazard of $\mathrm{SO_2}$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ dissolves in rain water to form sulphurous and then sulphuric acid, causing **acid rain**, which damages plants and buildings and acidifies rivers and lakes. (It is also a toxic gas that irritates the lungs and causes breathing problems.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one large scale use of $\mathrm{SO_3}$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Manufacture of **sulphuric acid** (the $\mathrm{SO_3}$ is dissolved in concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum, which is then diluted).
